{{nihongo|'''Fukami Shrine'''|深見神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Fukami, {{ill|Yamato, Kanagawa|ar|ياماتو (كاناغاوا)|azb|یاماتو، کاناقاوا|be|Ямата (горад)|bg|Ямато (град)|ca|Yamato (Kanagawa)|ce|Ямато (гӀала)|ceb|Yamato-shi|cs|Jamato (Kanagawa)|de|Yamato (Kanagawa)|eo|Jamato (Kanagavo)|es|Yamato (Kanagawa)|et|Yamato (Kanagawa)|fa|یاماتو، کاناگاوا|fi|Yamato (Kanagawa)|fr|Yamato (Kanagawa)|ga|Yamato|ie|Yamato (Kanagawa)|it|Yamato (Kanagawa)|ja|大和市|ko|야마토시|mzn|یاماتو، کاناگاوا|nl|Yamato (Kanagawa)|no|Yamato (Kanagawa)|pl|Yamato (Kanagawa)|pt|Yamato (Kanagawa)|ro|Yamato, Kanagawa|ru|Ямато (город)|sh|Jamato|simple|Yamato, Kanagawa|sr|Јамато (град)|sv|Yamato, Kanagawa|tg|Ямато|th|ยามาโตะ (จังหวัดคานางาวะ)|tl|Yamato, Kanagawa|tr|Yamato, Kanagawa|tt|Ямато (шәһәр)|uk|Ямато (Канаґава)|ur|یماٹو، کناگوا|uz|Yamato (Kanagawa)|vi|Yamato, Kanagawa|war|Yamato, Kanagawa|zh|大和市|zh_classical|大和市|zh_min_nan|Yamato-chhī|zh_yue|大和市|qid=Q386697}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|Q127513|qid=Q127513}}. It is regarded as one of the thirteen shrines listed in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}' (AD {{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}, {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5) for {{ill|Sagami Province|ckb|پارێزگای ساگامی|cs|Provincie Sagami|de|Provinz Sagami|es|Provincia de Sagami|fa|ولایت ساگامی|fr|Province de Sagami|gl|Provincia de Sagami|id|Provinsi Sagami|it|Sagami (provincia)|ja|相模国|ko|사가미국|lt|Sagamio žemė|nl|Sagami (provincie)|pt|Província de Sagami|ru|Сагами (провинция)|simple|Sagami Province|sk|Sagami (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сагами|tr|Sagami (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Саґамі|zh|相模國|zh_min_nan|Sagami-kok|zh_yue|相模國|qid=Q1053732}} (a minor shrine){{sfn|新編相模国風土記稿 深見村 鹿島社}}. Also, in the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}} gazetteer '{{ill|Shinpen Sagami no Kuni Fudoki-kō|Q11503942|qid=Q11503942}},' it is written as '''Kashima Shrine'''{{sfn|新編相模国風土記稿 深見村 鹿島社}}. {{nihongo|'''Fukami Shrine'''|深見神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Sagami Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
* {{ill|Kuraokami|Q644201|qid=Q644201|lt=Kuraokami no Kami}} (Kuraokami; rain deity)
*: Considered the original enshrined deity at the time of this shrine’s founding. In {{ill|2012|Q1990|qid=Q1990}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 24), it was merged from the precinct shrine Okura {{ill|Inari shrine|Q514480|qid=Q514480}}.
* {{ill|Takemikazuchi|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi}} (Takemikazuchi; deity of enduring martial fortune)
*: Said to have been {{ill|Bunrei|Q195793|qid=Q195793|lt=divided and invited}} from {{ill|Kashima Jingū|Q706499|qid=Q706499}} in {{ill|Hitachi Province|Q1055353|qid=Q1055353}} by the Sakamoto family, lords of {{ill|Fukami Domain|Q10863506|qid=Q10863506}} in the early Edo period, and has since been treated as this shrine’s deity. At that time, Kuraokami, formerly the deity of this shrine, is thought to have been merged into the precinct shrine Okura Inari.
* {{ill|Takeminakata|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata}} (Takeminakata)
*: In {{ill|1909|Q2057|qid=Q2057}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 42), merged on equal footing with this shrine’s deities from the extra-precinct {{ill|Massha|Q135009906|qid=Q135009906}} {{ill|Suwa Shrine|Q2370082|qid=Q2370082}} in Fukami.

:''For transitions in this shrine’s enshrined deities, see the later section “{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=#Changes in enshrined deities and origin of the alternate name “Kashima Shrine”}}.”''

== Origins and history ==
A fire in {{ill|1876|Q7766|qid=Q7766}} (Meiji 9)<ref name="kasai">From the “History” board in Fukami Shrine precincts and the official pamphlet 'Engishiki Fukami Shrine History.' Some sources, including the Kanagawa Association of Shrines website, say the fire occurred in “Meiji 8” ({{ill|1875|Q7764|qid=Q7764}}).</ref> destroyed everything from shrine buildings to {{ill|komonjo|Q89298567|qid=Q89298567}}. The following is the tradition transmitted at this shrine, but except for matters recorded in historical {{ill|historical document|Q3771738|qid=Q3771738}} such as the 'Sōkoku Fudoki' and the 'Engishiki Jinmyōchō,' it does not survive today as formal {{ill|Document|Q49848|qid=Q49848}} ({{ill|Historical source|Q3750478|qid=Q3750478}}).

== Beginnings of Fukami and this shrine (documents and shrine tradition) ==
According to the 'Sōkoku Fudoki,' it was “first enshrined in the 3rd month of the 22nd year of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Q357235|qid=Q357235}} ({{ill|478|Q30910|qid=Q30910}}),” but the exact founding date is unknown<ref name="kanagawajinja-guidebook">'Kanagawa Shrines Guidebook: A Stroll of the Heart' (Kanashin Publishing / supervised by Kanagawa Association of Shrines, Oct. 20, 1997), p.92</ref>. It also states that the deity enshrined then was “Kuraokami”<ref name="kanagawajinja-guidebook" />. On the other hand, before Takeminakata was merged in the Meiji period, Kuraokami had, through some process, been removed from the main hall’s deity lineup and became a deity of the precinct shrine Okura Inari; until that merger, only Takemikazuchi was the deity of this shrine (main hall) (for the currently prominent explanation of this process, see {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=below}}).

According to the theory of prefectural historic-site investigator Akira Ishino, the sea of {{ill|Sagami Bay|Q1061221|qid=Q1061221}} once extended deeply into this area, and transportation by {{ill|boat|Q4265275|qid=Q4265275}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=rafts}} was established (this {{ill|Inlet|Q1172599|qid=Q1172599}} is provisionally called the “Old Fukami Inlet”). Furthermore, as a collective name for the whole {{ill|Sakai River (Tokyo, Kanagawa)|Q6375268|qid=Q6375268|lt=Sakaigawa}} basin, Fukami was formerly written as “Deep Sea” or “Deep Water.” The place name Fukami first appears in literature in the '{{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|Q2702542|qid=Q2702542|lt=Wamyō Ruijushō}},' compiled in the {{ill|Jōhei|Q1324874|qid=Q1324874|lt=Jōhei}} era ({{ill|931|Q24789|qid=Q24789}}–{{ill|938|Q24794|qid=Q24794}}), where it is written as “Fukami-go, {{ill|Kōza District, Kanagawa|Q1202776|qid=Q1202776}}, Sagami Province”; here too it denotes a broader area than today’s locality<ref name="chosa" />.

In this shrine’s {{ill|Pratītyasamutpāda|Q522046|qid=Q522046}} (origin account), it is said that when Takemikazuchi (this shrine’s deity), whose purpose was pacification of the {{ill|Tōgoku|Q10343838|qid=Q10343838}}, advanced from Kashima in {{ill|Hitachi Province|Q1055353|qid=Q1055353|lt=Hitachi}} with a naval force ({{ill|boat corps|Q11129885|qid=Q11129885|lt=boat corps}}) into “deep sea,” the land was governed by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Izanagi}}’s child {{ill|Ukanomitama|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama}} and Kuraokami. Kuraokami, the rain deity, opened fertile rice fields and founded a settlement by local people. This is said to be the beginning of Fukami (both deities had been enshrined at Okura Inari in the precincts, but after Kuraokami was merged into the main hall, only Ukanomitama remains there today)<ref name="chosa" /><ref name="jinjyacho" />.

== Worship of this shrine ==
It has long been the center of worship for local people, and was particularly devoutly revered by figures including {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ar|ميناموتو نو يوريتومو|be|Мінамота-но Ёрытома|bg|Минамото но Йоритомо|br|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ca|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ckb|مینامۆتۆ نۆ یۆریتۆمۆ|cs|Joritomo Minamoto|de|Minamoto no Yoritomo|el|Μιναμότο νο Γιοριτόμο|eo|Minamoto no Yoritomo|es|Minamoto no Yoritomo|eu|Minamoto no Yoritomo|fa|میناموتو نو یوریتومو|fi|Minamoto no Yoritomo|fr|Minamoto no Yoritomo|hak|Minamoto no Yoritomo|he|מינאמוטו נו יוריטומו|hu|Minamoto no Joritomo|id|Minamoto no Yoritomo|it|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝|ko|미나모토노 요리토모|la|Minamoto no Yoritomo|lt|Minamoto no Joritomo|mr|मिनामोटो नो योरिमोटो|ms|Minamoto no Yoritomo|nl|Minamoto no Yoritomo|pl|Yoritomo Minamoto|pt|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ro|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ru|Минамото-но Ёритомо|sh|Minamoto no Yoritomo|sk|Joritomo Minamoto|sl|Minamoto no Joritomo|sq|Minamoto no Joritomo|sr|Минамото но Јоритомо|sv|Minamoto no Yoritomo|th|มินาโมโตะ โนะ โยริโตโมะ|tl|Minamoto no Yoritomo|tr|Minamoto no Yoritomo|uk|Мінамото-но Йорітомо|vi|Minamoto no Yoritomo|war|Minamoto no Yoritomo|wuu|源赖朝|zh|源赖朝|zh_min_nan|Minamoto no Yoritomo|zh_yue|源賴朝|zu|Minamoto no Yoritomo|qid=Q242800}}, the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Later Hōjō clan}}, {{ill|Takeda Shingen|Q276404|qid=Q276404}}, {{ill|Shibuya Shigekuni|Q11561779|qid=Q11561779|lt=Shibuya no Shōji Shigekuni}}, and {{ill|Ōta Dōkan|Q386144|qid=Q386144}}. During the {{ill|Siege of Osaka|Q475780|qid=Q475780}} under the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tokugawa shogunate}}, the {{ill|Hatamoto|Q572662|qid=Q572662}} {{ill|Sakamoto Shigeyasu|Q11425380|qid=Q11425380|lt=Sakamoto Kozayemon Shigeyasu}}, who prayed here for lasting martial fortune, also donated {{ill|Paddy field|Q842623|qid=Q842623}} at that time, and these remain as “Kashimada.” Furthermore, {{ill|Sakamoto Shigeharu|Q11425381|qid=Q11425381}}, Shigeyasu’s {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=adopted son}} and later {{ill|Jisha-bugyō|Q1036279|qid=Q1036279}}, is said to have repeatedly worshiped here, overseen construction of shrine buildings, and erected a shrine name marker inscribed “Sagami no Kuni, one of the thirteen seats: Fukami Shrine”<ref name="jinjyacho" />. The Sakamoto family were then the lords of Fukami.

== Since modern times ==
In {{ill|1873|ab|1873|af|1873|als|1873|am|1873 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1873|ar|1873|ary|1873|arz|1873|ast|1873|avk|1873|az|1873|azb|۱۸۷۳ (میلادی)|ba|1873 йыл|ban|1873|bar|1873|bat_smg|1873|bcl|1873|be|1873|be_x_old|1873|bg|1873|bn|১৮৭৩|bpy|মারি ১৮৭৩|br|1873|bs|1873.|ca|1873|cdo|1873 nièng|ce|1873 шо|ceb|1873|ckb|١٨٧٣|crh|1873|cs|1873|csb|1873|cv|1873|cy|1873|da|1873|de|1873|diq|1873|el|1873|eml|1873|eo|1873|es|1873|et|1873|eu|1873|fa|۱۸۷۳|fi|1873|fiu_vro|1873|fo|1873|fr|1873|frp|1873|frr|1873|fur|1873|fy|1873|ga|1873|gan|1873年|gcr|1873|gd|1873|gl|1873|gv|1873|he|1873|hi|१८७३|hif|1873|hr|1873.|hsb|1873|ht|1873 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1873|hy|1873|hyw|1873 թուական|ia|1873|id|1873|ilo|1873|inh|1873 шу|io|1873|is|1873|it|1873|ja|1873年|jv|1873|ka|1873|kaa|1873|kk|1873 жыл|kn|೧೮೭೩|ko|1873년|krc|1873 джыл|ku|1873|kv|1873-ӧд во|la|1873|lb|1873|lez|1873 йис|li|1873|lij|1873|lmo|1873|lt|1873 m.|lv|1873. gads|mai|१८७३|map_bms|1873|mdf|1873|mg|1873|mhr|1873|mi|1873|min|1873|mk|1873|ml|1873|mr|इ.स. १८७३|mrj|1873 и|ms|1873|my|၁၈၇၃|myv|1873 ие|mzn|۱۸۷۳|nah|1873|nap|1873|nds|1873|nds_nl|1873|new|ई सं १८७३|nl|1873|nn|1873|no|1873|nrm|1873|nso|1873|oc|1873|olo|1873|or|୧୮୭୩|os|1873-æм аз|pa|1873|pl|1873|pnb|1873|pt|1873|qu|1873|ro|1873|ru|1873 год|rue|1873|sa|१८७३|sah|1873 сыл|sc|1873|scn|1873|sd|1873ع|se|1873|sh|1873.|shn|1873|si|1873|simple|1873|sk|1873|sl|1873|smn|1873|sq|1873|sr|1873|stq|1873|su|1873|sv|1873|sw|1873|szl|1873|ta|1873|te|1873|tg|Соли 1873|th|พ.ศ. 2416|tk|1873|tl|1873|tly|1873|tr|1873|tt|1873 ел|udm|1873 ар|ug|1873 - يىلى|uk|1873|ur|1873ء|uz|1873|vec|1873|vi|1873|vls|1873|vo|1873|wa|1873|war|1873|wuu|1873年|xmf|1873|yi|1873|za|1873 nienz|zea|1873|zh|1873年|zh_classical|一八七三年|zh_min_nan|1873 nî|zh_yue|1873年|qid=Q7757}} (Meiji 6), by {{ill|Dajōkan Edict|Q11444008|qid=Q11444008|lt=Daijō-kan proclamation}}, it was ranked as a {{ill|Q712534|lt=village shrine}}. However, three years later in {{ill|1876|Q7766|qid=Q7766}} (Meiji 9)<ref name="kasai" />, it was devastated by a fire from neighboring {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Butsudō-ji}}; everything from shrine buildings to old documents burned, and it fell into ruin, with even its official rank becoming unclear. In {{ill|1909|Q2057|qid=Q2057}} (Meiji 42), it merged with the subsidiary Suwa Shrine that stood in Fukami’s Suwa-no-Mori, and Takeminakata was merged into this shrine on equal footing (aiden)<ref name="kanagawajinja-guidebook" />. At this stage there was only a temporary shrine building (kariden), with no main hall etc. built. Thereafter, recovery plans were made repeatedly but not realized; only in {{ill|1941|Q5231|qid=Q5231}} (Shōwa 16), 66 years after the fire, was it finally rebuilt at its current location (including the shrine buildings, {{ill|Torii|Q234731|qid=Q234731}}, and subsidiary shrines). The following year it was again ranked as a gōsha (the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former rank system}} was abolished in {{ill|1946|Q18610|qid=Q18610}} (Shōwa 21)){{R|"chosa"|"jinjyacho"}}.

In 2012 (Heisei 24), to commemorate the 70th anniversary of reconstruction, a new shrine name marker was erected, and Kuraokami—the deity listed in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'—was merged from Okura Inari into the main hall.

== Affiliated and subsidiary shrines ==
== Shrines within the precincts ==
[[File:Fukami-jinja-okura-to-yasukuni.JPG|thumb|250px|right|Okura Inari and Yasukuni-sha standing side by side]]
[[File:Fukami-jinja-torii(east).JPG|thumb|250px|right|Torii on the east side: said to be the original torii, and the old shrine buildings are thought to have stood near Okura Inari in a straight line from here]]
Okura Inari Shrine and Yasukuni-sha are enshrined on the west side of this shrine’s {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|Q3125745|qid=Q3125745}} in an east-facing row.
* Okura Inari Shrine (Okura Inari)
*: {{ill|Ukanomitama|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama}} is enshrined. Until 2012 (Heisei 24), Kuraokami—now a deity of the main hall—was also enshrined there. It is said to be the old shrine site of Fukami Shrine, and the haiden is said to have once stood near the Inari facing east (currently south-facing).
*: Note that shrine buildings at the current location were only constructed in 1941 (Shōwa 16)<ref name="chosa">[https://web.archive.org/web/20160304141429/http://www.geocities.jp/engisiki02/sagami/bun/sag160502-01.html Fukami Shrine] (Survey of Engishiki Shrines)</ref>.
* {{ill|Aviation Shrines|Q30319396|qid=Q30319396|lt=Yasukuni-sha}} (Atsugi Air Shrine, {{ill|Sessha|Q135009904|qid=Q135009904}})

Dünya Savaşı)|uk|Тихоокеанський театр воєнних дій Другої світової війни|ur|بحر الکاہل جنگ|uz|Tinch okeanidagi urush|vi|Chiến tranh Thái Bình Dương|wuu|太平洋战争|zh|太平洋战争|zh_min_nan|Thài-pêng-iûⁿ Chiàn-cheng|zh_yue|太平洋戰爭|qid=Q184425}}. After the war, when abolition was ordered, it was transferred on April 7, {{ill|1951|Q18591|qid=Q18591}} (Shōwa 26) to this shrine’s grounds, where local Fukami war dead were also merged<ref name="jinjyacho">[http://www.kanagawa-jinja.or.jp/search_dtl.php4?jid=660&cd=1207077&scd=&npg=0 Fukami Shrine] (Kanagawa Association of Shrines)</ref>.
* Tomizawa Inari Shrine
*: Strictly speaking, it cannot be directly reached from inside this shrine’s precincts (blocked by trees), but it stands at the southwest corner of the precinct area. The entrance is just south after passing this shrine’s west torii. It is thought to be an Inari shrine connected with the Tomizawa family, who established a {{ill|Silk throwing|Q7515235|qid=Q7515235|lt=silk reeling}} company in Fukami<ref>[http://53020342.at.webry.info/201010/article_13.html A journey beyond time and space to “Fukami Domain”] (Osanpo Seikatsu)</ref>.

== Changes in enshrined deities and origin of the alternate name “Kashima Shrine” ==
The 'Sōkoku Fudoki' says, “Enshrined in the 3rd month of the 22nd year of Emperor Yūryaku ({{ill|478|Q30910|qid=Q30910}}), and the deity is Kuraokami,” and the original deity is considered to have been Kuraokami.

On the other hand, the alternate name “Kashima Shrine” is said to come from the Sakamoto family, former local lords, having {{ill|Bunrei|Q195793|qid=Q195793|lt=invited a divided spirit}} of the deity of {{ill|Kashima Jingū|Q706499|qid=Q706499}} (now in {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|Q83273|qid=Q83273}}) to this shrine<ref name="kanagawajinja-guidebook" /><ref name="chosa" />. Takemikazuchi, one of this shrine’s deities, is said to have been enshrined at that time<ref>[http://www.yamato-kankou.com/%E3%82%84%E3%81%BE%E3%81%A8%E3%81%AE%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE/ Shrines of Yamato] (Yamato City Event & Tourism Association)</ref>, and the Kanagawa Association of Shrines / Kanagawa Shimbun 'Kanagawa Shrines Guidebook' explains that “after entering the Edo period, {{ill|Sakamoto Shigeyasu|Q11425380|qid=Q11425380|lt=Sakamoto Kozayemon Shigeyasu}} installed Takemikazuchi, a divided spirit of Kashima Jingū, as the enshrined deity<ref name="kanagawajinja-guidebook" /><ref>[http://members.jcom.home.ne.jp/nicepar-kaz90/kaz.osannpo.nikki04/3.htm Along the Sakaigawa II South Course] (Kaz’s Walking Diary)</ref>.”

At this time, Kuraokami, formerly the deity, is thought to have been merged into Okura Inari Shrine; from then on, only Takemikazuchi was treated as the deity of this shrine’s main hall. Later, as noted above, in 1909 (Meiji 42), as part of restoration after the shrine had fallen into ruin without rebuilding following the fire in 1876 (Meiji 9)<ref name="kasai" />, Takeminakata was merged from Suwa Shrine (a subsidiary shrine in the same area), and a temporary shrine hall was built in the precincts. Further, in 2012 (Heisei 24), Kuraokami—thought to be the original deity—was merged from Okura Inari, making the shrine’s deities three: Kuraokami, Takemikazuchi, and Takeminakata.

== Cultural properties in the precincts ==
{{seealso|List of designated cultural properties of Yamato City}}
* Fukami Shrine name marker (Yamato City designated Important {{ill|Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)|Q2901860|qid=Q2901860}}<ref>[http://www.city.yamato.lg.jp/web/kouhou/youranP32-33.html Yamato Catalog – Cultural Properties] (Yamato City)</ref>) - Erected in {{ill|1791|Q7784|qid=Q7784}} ({{ill|Kansei|Q1195131|qid=Q1195131}} 3). The front reads, “Sagami Province, one of thirteen seats, Fukami Shrine”{{sfn|新編相模国風土記稿 深見村 鹿島社}}. It is said to have been erected by {{ill|Sakamoto Shigeharu|Q11425381|qid=Q11425381|lt=Sakamoto Naiki Shigeharu}} (''born {{ill|1630|Q6856|qid=Q6856}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}} 7), died {{ill|1693|Q7689|qid=Q7689}} ({{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 6)''), head of the hatamoto Sakamoto family that ruled Fukami village through the Edo period and served as Commissioner of Temples and Shrines, briefly elevated to daimyō (lord of {{ill|Fukami Domain|Q10863506|qid=Q10863506}})<ref name="neko" />; however, the erection year above does not match Shigeharu’s active years.
* {{ill|Ulmus davidiana var. japonica|Q844010|qid=Q844010}} (Yamato City designated {{ill|Natural monument|Q23790|qid=Q23790}}<ref>[http://www.city.yamato.lg.jp/web/content/000133517.pdf List of designated cultural properties of Yamato City (PDF)] (Yamato City)</ref>) - A {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=sacred tree}} with a trunk circumference of 4 m and height of 43 m, said to be 500 years old. Since it normally grows naturally in {{ill|Highland|Q878223|qid=Q878223}}, growth in lowlands is rare nationwide. As its species was once unknown, the shrine has long called it the “{{ill|Nanjamonja tree|Q11324098|qid=Q11324098|lt=Nanjamonja tree}}.” In the past, on the north side of this tree, there was also a sacred “Engi Pine” said to be over 1,300 years old<ref name="jinjyacho" />{{sfn|新編相模国風土記稿 深見村 鹿島社}}.

== Other ==
== Fukami Shrine South Site ==
Prior to construction of the [https://web.archive.org/web/20040607235323/http://homepage3.nifty.com/c-fukamiminami/index.html Yamato City Community Center Fukami Minami Hall], an {{ill|Archaeological excavation|Q959782|qid=Q959782}} for record preservation was conducted from April to July {{ill|1988|Q2426|qid=Q2426}} (Shōwa 63). This survey discovered one {{ill|Archaeological excavation|Q959782|qid=Q959782}} from the {{ill|Nara period|Q189178|qid=Q189178}}, four pit dwellings and two {{ill|Post in ground|Q1695743|qid=Q1695743}} from the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, and two ditch-like {{ill|Feature (archaeology)|Q814254|qid=Q814254}} from the {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}. In addition to artifacts from these features, {{ill|Stone tool|Q479257|qid=Q479257}} from the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Paleolithic}} and {{ill|Jōmon period|Q52824|qid=Q52824}} were also found<ref name="fukamijinjya-minamiiseki">[http://www.city.yamato.lg.jp/web/shakai/annaiban.html Cultural Property Guide Boards in Yamato City] “Fukami Shrine South Site” (the guide board is located southwest of the [https://web.archive.org/web/20040607235323/http://homepage3.nifty.com/c-fukamiminami/index.html Yamato City Community Center Fukami Minami Hall] in 1-chome Fukamidai, Yamato City)</ref>.

; Pit-dwelling Structure No. 5
Pit-dwelling Structure No. 5 (rectangular plan, 3.7 m × 3.5 m, about 0.3 m deep) is a late- to end-9th-century Heian-period feature. It had been damaged by the ditch feature mentioned above, and {{ill|Column|Q4817|qid=Q4817}} and {{ill|Roof|Q83180|qid=Q83180}} did not survive, but it had a {{ill|Kamado|Q12177411|qid=Q12177411}} on the east side and an underfloor {{ill|Prehistoric storage pits|Q1421012|qid=Q1421012}} lined with {{ill|Clay|Q42302|qid=Q42302}} (purpose unknown; it was filled during use of the building). Many earthenware vessels used as everyday {{ill|household utensils|Q11376286|qid=Q11376286}} were excavated from inside the building remains. No other remains from the same period were found, but further surveys in surrounding areas are expected to clarify the full picture of the {{ill|Human settlement|Q486972|qid=Q486972}}<ref name="fukamijinjya-minamiiseki"/>.
